findings.reason: The protected solution is concise, conventional, and interview-ready. It greedily orients every intact block, isolates the one block containing the cut, tries both of that block's orientations, and enumerates each cut position with direct lexicographic comparison. The names oriented, middle, split_word, cut, candidate, and best make the construction self-explanatory.

For a fixed split block, every other block appears intact at a fixed candidate position, so replacing it independently by its lexicographically larger orientation cannot worsen the full string. The split block is the only exception because its suffix becomes the prefix; trying both orientations and every character cut therefore enumerates an optimum. The middle concatenation preserves the original circular block order.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 555 and its Python splitLoopedString(strs) interface. The app-local solve(strs) contract preserves every character once, never permutes blocks, permits a cut inside any block, and returns exactly one lexicographically maximal lowercase string of total input length.

The protected app source and immutable native source bound to verified submission 2065368263 are algorithmically identical: both compute max(value, reversed value) for intact blocks, build the following-plus-preceding middle, test both split-block orientations, rotate at every cut, and retain the largest candidate.

The three one-character-string workloads span total lengths 3 through 12 and make reversal choices semantically duplicate while still forcing a naive orientation-vector enumerator through 2^L combinations. The exact protected source passed all 11 refreshed correctness cases and all three performance tiers, including both legal 1,000-character boundaries. The correct exponential control passed every benchmark output but failed only scaling with relative growth exponent +4.38 and a 710.72x largest runtime ratio.

The Approach exactly matches the current target and explains why only the split block needs both orientations. Its complexity section now defines L as the total character count and correctly derives O(L^2) time from L cuts with length-L construction/comparison and O(L) auxiliary space.

The modular Reference was reviewed directly in the authenticated Premium statement and bound to its rendered live-content hash. It preserves the orientation and breakpoint phases, fixed block order, both source examples, all four orientation loops and the cut reasoning in Example 1, and all four constraints.

coverage: Both authenticated Premium source examples appear first and in source order with their exact string arrays and lexicographically maximal outputs.
The invented palindrome sample was relabelled as a trial, and the formerly hidden mixed-string, competing-orientation, and palindromic-middle cases are now visible trials.
Contract boundaries cover one character, one 1,000-character string, 1,000 one-character strings, and total length 1,000 while retaining only nonempty lowercase words.

Material semantics cover independent block reversal, fixed circular block order, cuts inside a block, cuts between one-character blocks, both orientations of the split block, greedy intact-block orientation, palindromes, mirrored strings, and repeated maximum candidates.

Exhaustive orientation-vector and circular-rotation enumeration verified the nine non-maximum correctness cases and all three benchmark outputs. Direct witnesses establish both maximum outputs, and the protected app and immutable native sources also agreed on 2,954 exhaustive small lists and 1,000 randomized lists.
All eleven correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged 3-, 6-, and 12-character one-character-block workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
